summary: Running the documented 'make test-fast' inside the learner's installation writes a test trace (request_id req-bad-payload, capability unknown.write, canonical_outcome AMBIGUOUS, needs_attention true, 45 attempts) into the installation's own operations/diagnostics/traces.jsonl; 'los operations' then reports it as an operation needing attention.
expected: README.md 'Commands' lists make test-fast as 'quick feedback: synthetic fixtures, no checked-in repository load', i.e. tests isolated from the learner's installation state; OPERATOR.md treats 'los operations' as the record of this installation's requests.
actual: operations/diagnostics/traces.jsonl did not exist before (S01-before snapshot shows only .gitkeep); after make test-fast it has 135 lines, first span at 2026-09-25T00:17:29Z (during the test run). 'los operations' lists trace bff87904f6d407966d784832196f7e19 / req-bad-payload with needs_attention true. Harness follow-up after S01 (same world, TRACEPARENT unset so every request gets its own trace): a second make test-fast appended another 135 trace lines, and 'los operations' then listed 20 operations (its first page), all canonical_outcome AMBIGUOUS and needs_attention true, one per capability (req-stage.note.write, req-stage.progress.update, req-review.apply, req-project.create, ...). The leak therefore does not depend on TRACEPARENT; TRACEPARENT only merged the first run's requests into one entry.
reproduction: .venv/bin/python tools/los.py operations   # shows req-bad-payload, AMBIGUOUS, needs_attention true
own_error_possible: Running the test suite inside a learner's live installation may not be an intended use, but README lists make test-fast among the ordinary commands without warning, and the scenario asked to confirm the tooling works.

summary: 'make test-fast' fails 34 of 2278 selected tests on a healthy installation (validator 0 errors); at least 16 failures are FileNotFoundError on files of another learner's workspace (work/active/workspace-m2-exam-prep/outputs/sad-l06|l11-chapter-summaries/...), others are assertion failures in operations ordering, recovery conflicts, causal resolver and diagnostic store tests.
expected: README.md: 'make test-fast  # quick feedback: synthetic fixtures, no checked-in repository load' — a portable green check of the tooling.
actual: exit 2 after 10m51s: '34 failed, 2214 passed, 30 skipped, 83 deselected in 651.13s'. Re-run with TRACEPARENT unset: '30 failed, 2218 passed, 30 skipped, 83 deselected in 649.70s' — the four tests/test_operations.py failures disappear (they were caused by the agent environment's inherited TRACEPARENT); 30 remain: 17 test_pilot_replay (FileNotFoundError on another learner's workspace-m2-exam-prep files), 5 test_causal_resolver, 2 test_diagnostic_store, 3 test_recovery_conflicts, 1 test_abilities, 1 test_format_fixtures, 1 test_gateway_v2.
own_error_possible: The eval world replaces the original author's learner data with a synthetic history; tests pinned to the author's data would fail in any other learner's installation too, which is what a consumer experiences. Timing-sensitive tests may also be affected by this 4-core container. 4 of the 34 original failures were caused by the inherited TRACEPARENT of this agent environment, not by the product.

summary: 'make setup' with the default interpreter (python3 = 3.11) fails in pip and leaves a half-built .venv; the README's documented override 'make setup PYTHON=python3.x' then fails the same way because the stale .venv/bin/python still points at 3.11. Only deleting .venv by hand recovers.
expected: README.md: 'Build with a specific interpreter via make setup PYTHON=python3.14' and 'the tools fail fast with the setup command if a dependency is missing or too old'.
actual: make setup -> exit 2 (pip: requires a different Python: 3.11.15 not in '>=3.12'); make setup PYTHON=python3.12 -> exit 2 with the identical error; pyvenv.cfg says 3.12 but .venv/bin/python3 -> /usr/local/bin/python3 (3.11).
reproduction: on a machine whose python3 is 3.11 and python3.12 exists
own_error_possible: A more experienced user would pass PYTHON= on the first try; but the Makefile default and the README both lead to the failing path first.

summary: 'los operations' merges independent gateway requests that inherit the same W3C TRACEPARENT from the environment into one 'operation' and misreports a committed write: after a refused request (s04-a09-stage-note-1) and a separate committed request (s04-a09-stage-note-2, receipt transaction-20260925-003709-001), it lists one operation named after the refused request with attempts 2, canonical_outcome AMBIGUOUS, recovery_requirement reconcile-exact-request, needs_attention true.
expected: OPERATOR.md/CONSUMER-PROTOCOL treat 'los operations' as the record of request/trace ids; distinct request_ids with distinct outcomes, and a committed write with a receipt, should not be reported as an ambiguous needs-attention operation.
actual: Both processes wrote spans with trace_id/operation_id bff87904f6d407966d784832196f7e19 (the value of the agent environment's TRACEPARENT). The same id also labelled the S01 test-suite trace in another world. With TRACEPARENT unset, each request gets its own trace and 'los operations' lists them separately.
reproduction: submit any two capability envelopes with different request_id/idempotency_key (e.g. two capture.create envelopes with a wrong approval hash)
los operations   # one operation, attempts 2, request_id of the first
repeat with 'env -u TRACEPARENT' -> two separate operations
own_error_possible: TRACEPARENT is injected by the agent harness, not set by me; adopting an inherited trace context is standard tracing behaviour. The defect is that the product uses the inherited trace id as the identity of one logical operation and derives outcome/needs_attention across unrelated requests, which any agent or CI environment exporting TRACEPARENT will hit.
